steps.prompt:
Create a polished character-modeling reference sheet of EXACTLY the same Sprig character in the provided reference, shown from FOUR SIDES in a clean 2 by 2 grid. This is a turnaround of the approved character, NOT a redesign. Preserve the extremely large rounded-square pale warm pistachio face, huge warm dark brown eyes, tiny button nose, happy open mouth with tongue INSIDE mouth, rosy cheeks, tiny plump body, very short legs, green feet, broad sculpted stylized leaf hair and leaf collar. Preserve the strong ASYMMETRIC swept crown: one very large diagonal broad leaf across forehead points upward toward the viewer's right in the front view, with the same few smaller overlapping leaves over the other temple and matching broad side and lower cheek leaves. Soft premium 3D mobile game aesthetic, sculpted leaf folds, satin materials, simplified veins, no realistic foliage or thin noisy veins.

Layout: TOP LEFT strict orthographic FRONT (looking straight at viewer); TOP RIGHT strict orthographic RIGHT SIDE (nose pointing right on the sheet); BOTTOM LEFT strict orthographic LEFT SIDE (nose pointing left); BOTTOM RIGHT strict orthographic BACK. Small unobtrusive gray captions FRONT / RIGHT / LEFT / BACK below each corresponding figure. Equal full-body scale and same proportions, neutral very light warm plain background. Each figure fully visible with generous clear margins, no cropping any leaf or fingertip. No scenery, props, turntable base, logos, dimensions, arrows or watermark.

Use a clean modeling T-POSE in all four panels: arms straight out sideways at shoulder height, elbows straight, relaxed open hands, legs slightly separated, head upright. Exactly FOUR digits per hand: three short rounded simple fingers plus a separate thumb, coherent natural symmetrical hand anatomy, no extra fingers or twisted fingers. Front view palms forward, back view backs of hands visible. In true side views the outstretched arms point along camera axis and should be naturally FORESHORTENED (do not turn the body into a three-quarter view just to show arms). Same character physically rotated, same fixed expression and geometry, don't mirror-reinvent asymmetry. Back view shows reverse surfaces of the SAME crown and a clean green rear head; no eyes, nose, mouth or duplicated face on rear. Leaf collar wraps around the neck, central chest bib only on front. Keep the little body and giant head from the reference, not a taller humanoid or a spherical lettuce costume. Crisp clear modeling reference, very soft grounding shadow, consistent neutral bright studio lighting.

Refine this exact Sprig FOUR-VIEW turnaround reference sheet. Keep the FRONT at top left and BACK at bottom right identical in character design, colors, proportions, framing, scale and pose. Keep the 2x2 layout, clean cream background and small captions FRONT, RIGHT, LEFT, BACK. Only correct the TWO SIDE PANELS to TRUE EXACT 90 DEGREE ORTHOGRAPHIC PROFILE views. TOP RIGHT faces right, BOTTOM LEFT faces left. The current sides are slightly three-quarter views: correct this by physically rotating the SAME character to exactly 90 degrees from front, not by simply removing the far eye. In each side view ONLY ONE EYE and ONE EYEBROW are visible. The far eye, far eyebrow, far cheek and far half of the mouth must be fully occluded by the head volume. Side profile nose is at the outer face silhouette, one cheek, mouth seen from the side. True side-facing body and feet, no three-quarter torso. T-pose arms point directly toward/away from the side camera, strongly foreshortened with near hand palm edge-on to head/torso area. Preserve exactly four digits per hand, three fingers plus thumb, no extra digits. Preserve the same distinctive asymmetrical layered broad leaf quiff and tiny plump body from the sheet. Crown and collar must rotate consistently with the head and torso; keep crown volume and stylized green sculpted leaf planes. Back remains faceless with green rear head and smaller rear collar leaves. Full-body characters no cropping. This is a modeling reference, so precise profile orientation is more important than seeing both eyes or both arms. Bright soft studio lighting matching the input, no other changes.
